newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares seen higher on Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares seen higher on Q1 results.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are expected to be higher in early trade on Friday with first quarter results of some major companies likely to boost sentiment, brokers said.
They said the rise in the Dow Jones on Thursday as Wall Street welcomed plans to lower the capital gains tax rate could also provide further stimulus to the market.
"Announcement of first quarter results by some companies are sound and better than our expectations. They will attract buyers' attention," one local broker said.
Lippo Securities and Lippo Life of the Lippo Group and Bank BNI were likely to reap positive sentiment on announcements of rises in Q1 net profits, brokers said.
Blue chip Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) announced that it posted a net profit of 115.4 billion rupiah in the first quarter 1997, a rise of 11.4 percent from its first quarter net profit in 1996.

Telecommunications firm Telkom and conglomerate Bimantara were likely to attract buyers on news reports that a multimedia firm, in which both firms holds share, will start operations in 1998, brokers said.

Wednesday's announcement of a healthy February trade surplus and a moderate rise in April prices coupled with reports that Indonesia foreign exchange reserves had reached a high of $20.38 billion were evidence that the economy was in good shape, analysts and brokers said.
On Wednesday, the Jakarta composite index rose 7.24 points, or 1.10 percent, to close at a day high of 666.84 points. The market was closed on Thursday for a public holiday.
